mechanism_narrative: The four-week decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES, paired with falling RESIDENTIAL time, signals a broad reopening of out-of-home routines that should keep lifting RETAIL_REC over the next month as commuting and discretionary trips continue to recover.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not remain above its last-4-week mean while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue to improve for another four weeks, the trend-signal claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM rises above +15 while PARKS stay below -30, households are shifting more of their errands into short, local trips that spill over into nearby retail visits, pushing RETAIL_REC upward over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above +15 and PARKS remains below -30
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to improve within two weeks after GROCERY_PHARM exceeds +15 while PARKS stays below -30, the threshold mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT continues falling faster than WORKPLACES, then access friction is still rising for shopping trips; that should depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks because fewer commuters convert travel time into retail visits.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls at least 5 points below WORKPLACES week-on-week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat for four weeks despite TRANSIT weakening relative to WORKPLACES, the access-friction claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS alongside falling RESIDENTIAL indicates more outdoor leisure and less at-home substitution, which should modestly raise RETAIL_REC within one week as weekend and evening foot traffic broadens.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase within one week while PARKS rises and RESIDENTIAL falls, the leisure-spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Once WORKPLACES moves back toward zero and TRANSIT remains less negative, weekday activity normalization should translate into higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks through lunchtime and after-work purchases.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -20 and TRANSIT rises above -25
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not outperform its prior four-week average after both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT cross the stated levels, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in GROCERY_PHARM above zero with little change in TRANSIT implies errand consolidation around essential shopping, which should pull RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks as consumers combine trip purposes.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above 0 while TRANSIT changes by less than 5 points
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not improve within two weeks under stable TRANSIT and positive GROCERY_PHARM, the consolidation mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Under reopening, a continuing decline in RESIDENTIAL time together with easing in TRANSIT indicates reduced stay-at-home pressure and easier circulation, which should increase RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC remains below its last-28-day mean despite further RESIDENTIAL declines and TRANSIT improvement, the reopening claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS keeps recovering while GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated, weekend outings and neighborhood errands should reinforce each other and lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks; the effect is strongest when both series rise together.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -30 and GROCERY_PHARM stays above +10
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise over four weeks when PARKS is above -30 and GROCERY_PHARM stays above +10, the interaction effect is rejected.
